key_insight: Individualized AI models combining wearable signals predicted perceived exertion better than pulse-rate-only models in patients with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).
clinical_relevance: Multimodal wearables could support exertion monitoring during ESKD prehabilitation, where limited physical capacity and beta-blocker use can make pulse rate less informative.
method: Collected smartwatch pulse rate, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data during prehabilitation.
Compared individualized pulse-rate-only regression models with multi-feature models predicting Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE).
Examined selected features to identify signals contributing beyond pulse rate.
evidence_signal: Among 13 ESKD patients and 13 healthy older controls, multi-feature models significantly improved ESKD prediction, achieving an RPE root mean square error of 1.33.
watch_item: The small cohort and individualized modeling require broader validation before clinical deployment; predicting perceived exertion does not establish monitoring safety.
paper_title: Wearable Sensors Predict Exertion Without Changes in Pulse Rate for Frail End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients
